# MDL003 mdl-include-cycle

The include graph has a cycle.

## What it does

The offending include is skipped so the rest of the model still loads. A diamond is not a cycle.

## Why it matters

An include cycle has no load order. Grimble breaks it by skipping one include, so which file wins would otherwise depend on traversal order.

## Remedy

Move the shared declarations into a file both sides include, and remove the back edge.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```grmb expect=fire file=design/model.grmb config="cycle"
grimble = "2";
module m;
include "b.grmb";
```

### Clean case 2

```grmb expect=clean file=design/model.grmb config="shared"
grimble = "2";
module m;
include "shared.grmb";
```

## Examples

### MDL003 include cycle / Two files including each other fire #1 (line 6) (fire)

```text
grimble = "2";
module m;
include "a.grmb";
=== design/a.grmb
grimble = "2";
part of m;
include "b.grmb";
=== design/b.grmb
grimble = "2";
part of m;
include "a.grmb";
```

### MDL003 include cycle / A diamond is not a cycle #2 (line 22) (clean)

```text
grimble = "2";
module m;
include "b.grmb";
include "c.grmb";
=== design/b.grmb
grimble = "2";
part of m;
include "d.grmb";
=== design/c.grmb
grimble = "2";
part of m;
include "d.grmb";
=== design/d.grmb
grimble = "2";
part of m;
node leaf : trusted {
}
```
